In [[cryptography]], '''Zodiac''' is a [[block cipher]] designed in 2000 by Chang-Hyi Lee for the Korean firm SoftForum.

Zodiac uses a 16-round [[Feistel cipher|Feistel network]] structure with [[key whitening]]. The round function uses only [[XOR]]s and [[substitution box|S-box]] lookups. There are two 8×8-bit S-boxes: one based on the discrete [[exponentiation]] 45<sup>''x''</sup> as in [[Secure and Fast Encryption Routine|SAFER]], the other using the [[multiplicative inverse]] in the [[finite field]] GF(2<sup>8</sup>), as introduced by [[SHARK]].

Zodiac is theoretically vulnerable to [[impossible differential cryptanalysis]], which can recover a 128-bit key in 2<sup>119</sup> encryptions.
